notes: Jeitun (Djeitun) culture of the Kopet Dag piedmont; the page says 'The settlement was occupied from about 7200 to 4500 BC possibly with short interruptions' and that the culture 'may have begun prior to 7000 BC'. The Namazga-Depe page's table gives 'Neolithic of Jeitun type 6200-5000 BCE'; the 4500 end of the Jeitun page is used because the Anau page begins the Anau culture at 4500 BC and says 'Jeitun period of Turkmenistan was followed by the Anau culture' (disagreement). The dossier starts at -6000. Extent: 'Sites are found on both sides of the Kopet Dag mountains', 'extend west as far as Shahrud, Iran, and east to the Tedjen river'; the type site 'covers an area of about 5,000 square meters'. Five discs (Ashgabat, Tejen, Quchan, Bojnurd, Shahrud) are drawn, a placement (confidence 2). The infobox's 'major sites' list also names Tepe Guran, Tepe Sarab and Ganj Dareh, which the page links through artefacts to 'Zagros sites such as Jarmo', and Yarim Tepe and Tureng Tepe; none is drawn, as they are outside the Kopet Dag range the page describes. Successor: the Anau culture (page: 'followed by the Anau culture'). The Iranian side has no successor on any page opened and goes to nobody. The Kelteminar page lists the Jeitun as the Kelteminar's predecessor (infobox 'Preceded by: Jeitun culture'): a relation to the north (Karakum, Amu Darya deltas) that no page dates. No Cliopatria shape, no area comparison.
